I wrote "Answer: False is less common before 2023-09-09" to `/work/answer.txt`. It is a close call, and I'm not certain of it.

The data has no labels, so I had to infer them. Each line pairs a word with a definition and a hedging phrase such as "may not be" or "is never". I treated a pair as a true match when it appeared two or more times. I treated it as a mismatch when the word or the definition appeared in a repeated pair with something else. A line is labelled False when its negation and its match status disagree.

- **Unclassified lines:** 524 of the 2,758 lines fit neither rule, so I left them out.
- **False share:** Of the lines I could classify, False was 53.2% before 2023-09-09 and 54.1% after.
- **Raw counts:** False was also lower before the date, 551 against 648.
- **Single line on the date:** One False line falls exactly on 2023-09-09 and was excluded.

The gap is under one percentage point, so the 524 excluded lines or a few misparsed ones could flip it.
